title: The meeting that should have been an email
text: Office workers {{1}} long joked that the typical meeting should have been an email. Research suggests they have a point: the average middle manager spends more than {{2}} of the working week in meetings, and studies find that decisions made in groups are often slower and no better. A large part of the problem is that discussion gets dominated {{3}} the loudest voice rather than the strongest argument, and the larger the group, {{4}} weaker each participant's sense of responsibility for the outcome. {{5}} is hard to argue with a meeting invitation, even {{6}} the diary suggests otherwise. Some companies, {{7}} calendars turned treacly during the pandemic years, have responded boldly: no meetings on certain days, shorter default slots, and agendas circulated {{8}} advance so that the reading happens before the talking.

gaps.explanation: Present perfect with a plural subject: have long joked.

gaps.hint: quantifier: more than ___ of the week
gaps.explanation: 'More than half of' — the fraction of the week.
Passive agent: dominated by the voice.

gaps.hint: article: the larger the group, ___ weaker
gaps.explanation: 'The larger…, the weaker…' — the double comparative needs 'the'.

gaps.hint: dummy subject: ___ is hard to argue
gaps.explanation: 'It is hard to…' — the dummy subject before the infinitive.

gaps.hint: conjunction: even ___ the diary suggests otherwise

gaps.explanation: 'Whose' links the companies to their calendars.
